title: Managing Warehouse Robots Like a Computer Network
hints: Warehouse-like map: plan robot moves to finish as many orders as possible
Approach: borrow ideas from computer networks
en: Good afternoon, everyone. Our project works on the **League of Robot Runners 2026** problem, or **LoRR** for short. We study **a warehouse-like map**: how to plan the robots' moves so that they **finish as many orders as possible**. Our approach borrows ideas from **computer networks**.
zh: 大家下午好。我们的项目做的是 **2026 年机器人跑者联赛（LoRR）** 的问题。我们研究的是：在一张**类似仓库的地图**上，怎么安排机器人走路，让它们**完成尽可能多的派单任务**。我们的做法是借用**计算机网络**的思路。

segs.en: Good afternoon, everyone. Our project works on the **League of Robot Runners 2026** problem, or **LoRR** for short.
segs.zh: 大家下午好。我们的项目做的是 **2026 年机器人跑者联赛（LoRR）** 的问题。

segs.en: We study **a warehouse-like map**: how to plan the robots' moves so that they **finish as many orders as possible**.
segs.zh: 我们研究的是：在一张**类似仓库的地图**上，怎么安排机器人走路，让它们**完成尽可能多的派单任务**。

segs.en: Our approach borrows ideas from **computer networks**.
segs.zh: 我们的做法是借用**计算机网络**的思路。

title: The task: hundreds of robots, narrow doors
en: First, the competition. Amazon Robotics sponsors it, and 2026 is its third year. 【指左图】 Each grey dot is a robot. For **5,000 ticks**, robots pick up and deliver orders. The score is **how many orders they finish**. 【指右边 1、2、3】 Every tick, the program makes **three choices**: which robot takes which order, which way it goes, and whether its next step can go now. 【指下方数字】 We use the official room map: **16 rooms and 31 doors**. Most doors are **one cell wide**. There are **200 to 300 robots**. 【指蓝色路线】 This one order goes through **eight doors**.
zh: 先介绍比赛：它由亚马逊机器人赞助，2026 年是第三届。【指左图】每个灰点是一台车。在 **5000 拍**里，车不停地取货、送货。比的是**完成多少单**。【指右边 1、2、3】程序每一拍做**三个决定**：哪台车接哪单、走哪条路、下一步现在能不能走。【指下方数字】我们用官方房间图：**16 个房间、31 道门**，大多数门只有**一格宽**，车有 **200 到 300 台**。【指蓝色路线】这一单就要穿过 **8 道门**。

segs.zh: 【指蓝色路线】这一单就要穿过 **8 道门**。

title: The longer it runs, the slower it gets
en: First, we ran the existing programs: the official starter program and the 2024 champion's order assignment. 【指三组曲线】 We saw something strange: **the longer it runs, the slower it gets.** Every curve goes down. 【指左边 127 和 37】 With the champion's assignment, over 60 runs, finished orders per 500 ticks fell from **127 at the start to 37 at the end**. That is less than one third. And there were **no errors and no collisions**. Every robot followed its plan. So no single robot was broken. **Something was building up over time.** Speaker 2 will show you what it was.
zh: 我们先跑了现有的程序：官方起始程序和 2024 届冠军的派单。【指三组曲线】我们看到一个奇怪的现象：**跑得越久，越慢。** 每条曲线都在往下掉。【指左边 127 和 37】用冠军派单，60 局平均，每 500 拍完成的单数从**开局 127 单降到最后 37 单**，不到三分之一。而且**没有报错、没有碰撞**，每台车都按计划走。所以不是哪台车坏了，而是**有什么东西在随时间累积**。下面讲者 2 讲累积的是什么。

title: Robots jam at one narrow door
figs: 图 3 第 3000 拍堵门截图
hints: Tick 3,000: 97 robots still have to cross door 6 inward (incl. not yet at the door)
Face to face in a 1-cell door
en: Thank you. To find out, we watched the replay tick by tick. 【指左图黑圈】 This is tick 3,000. **97 robots** have orders that still need to go through **one door, door 6**, into the lower-left rooms. Some are already waiting at the door. The others are still on the way. 【指右边第二张卡】 Why? Easy orders get done first. So more and more of the orders left must go through this door: from **38 percent up to 86 percent**. 【指第三张卡】 Then robots meet **face to face** in a one-cell door. In the second half, only **3.4 to 7 robots** get through every 500 ticks. When the door is in order, **26** get through. **More robots, fewer crossings.**
zh: 谢谢。为了弄清楚累积的是什么，我们一拍一拍地看回放。【指左图黑圈】这是第 3000 拍。手上任务还要穿过**同一道门，门 6**，进左下房间的车有 **97 台**：有的已经堵在门口，有的还在路上。【指右边第二张卡】为什么？好做的单先做完，剩下的单里要过这道门的越来越多：从 **38% 涨到最多 86%**。【指第三张卡】于是车在一格宽的门口**面对面顶住**。后半程每 500 拍只过 **3.4 到 7 台**，而门口有序时能过 **26 台**。**车越多，过得越少。**

title: Prior work misses one number
hints: 4 groups: assignment / route guidance / PIBT planners / congestion handling
Each does its own step well
One door → spreading traffic cannot help
Starter already has route guidance, still slows
Missing: count robots heading for the door, at assignment
en: Many people have worked on this. 【依次指四张卡】 Their methods fall into four groups. **Order assignment** picks orders that are close and cheap. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread to other roads. **Planners like PIBT** decide who moves first and avoid collisions. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle. 【指红字 Gap here】 But on this map, each one has a gap. The lower-left rooms have only one door, so spreading robots to other roads cannot help. The starter program already uses route guidance, and it still slows down. 【指底部黄框】 In the methods we read, **no one counts, when orders are given out, how many robots already have an order that must go through this door in this direction.**
zh: 当然，这个问题前人研究了很多年。【依次指四张卡】前人的方法分四类。**派单**挑近的、便宜的单；**选路**给拥挤的路加代价，让车分散到别的路；**PIBT 这类规划**决定谁先走、避免碰撞；**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着。【指红字 Gap here】但放到这张图上都有缺口：左下房间只有一道门，分流没有用；官方起始程序本身就带选路引导，照样变慢。【指底部黄框】在我们读到的方法里，**没有一种在派单时去数：已经接了要往这个方向过这道门的单的车有多少。**

segs.en: Many people have worked on this. 【依次指四张卡】 Their methods fall into four groups.
segs.zh: 当然，这个问题前人研究了很多年。【依次指四张卡】前人的方法分四类。

segs.en: **Order assignment** picks orders that are close and cheap. **Route guidance** makes busy roads cost more, so robots spread to other roads. **Planners like PIBT** decide who moves first and avoid collisions. **Jam handling** keeps some robots idle.
segs.zh: **派单**挑近的、便宜的单；**选路**给拥挤的路加代价，让车分散到别的路；**PIBT 这类规划**决定谁先走、避免碰撞；**拥堵处理**让一部分车闲着。

segs.en: 【指红字 Gap here】 But on this map, each one has a gap. The lower-left rooms have only one door, so spreading robots to other roads cannot help. The starter program already uses route guidance, and it still slows down.
segs.zh: 【指红字 Gap here】但放到这张图上都有缺口：左下房间只有一道门，分流没有用；官方起始程序本身就带选路引导，照样变慢。

segs.en: 【指底部黄框】 In the methods we read, **no one counts, when orders are given out, how many robots already have an order that must go through this door in this direction.**
segs.zh: 【指底部黄框】在我们读到的方法里，**没有一种在派单时去数：已经接了要往这个方向过这道门的单的车有多少。**

title: Our idea: treat the warehouse as a computer network
hints: Door = link; order through 8 doors = packet through 8 routers; jam = congestion
Why networks: decades on shared links; mature algorithms; we are CS students
en: The replay made us think of a computer network. 【指左边三行】 **A door is like a link** that can carry only so much. **An order going through eight doors is like a packet going through eight routers.** And **more robots but fewer crossings looks like network congestion**. 【指右边 1、2、3】 We picked computer networks for three reasons. First, networks have faced this problem for **decades**: many senders sharing a few links. Second, the field is **mature**. It has many tested methods for **routing**, which path to take, and **scheduling**, who goes when. Third, **we study computer science**. We know these methods, and also what they assume. 【指底部深色框】 So our guess was: **borrow routing and scheduling methods from networks, and the robots may finish more orders.** It was only a guess, so we had to test it. Speaker 3 will now explain the model and what we borrowed.
zh: 回放让我们想到计算机网络。【指左边三行】**门像一条链路**，能过的量有限；**一单穿过 8 道门，像数据包经过 8 台路由器**；**车越多、过门越少，像网络拥塞**。【指右边 1、2、3】选计算机网络有三个原因。第一，这个领域花了**几十年**解决的正是同一个问题：很多发送者共用少数几条线路。第二，它很**成熟**，有大量检验过的**路由**（走哪条路）和**调度**（谁什么时候走）方法。第三，**我们是计算机专业的学生**，熟悉这些方法，也熟悉它们的前提。【指底部深色框】所以我们的猜想是：**借用网络的路由和调度方法，车队也许能完成更多的单。** 这只是猜想，要靠实验检验。下面由讲者 3 讲模型和我们借了什么。

segs.zh: 回放让我们想到计算机网络。【指左边三行】**门像一条链路**，能过的量有限；**一单穿过 8 道门，像数据包经过 8 台路由器**；**车越多、过门越少，像网络拥塞**。

segs.en: 【指右边 1、2、3】 We picked computer networks for three reasons. First, networks have faced this problem for **decades**: many senders sharing a few links. Second, the field is **mature**. It has many tested methods for **routing**, which path to take, and **scheduling**, who goes when. Third, **we study computer science**. We know these methods, and also what they assume.
segs.zh: 【指右边 1、2、3】选计算机网络有三个原因。第一，这个领域花了**几十年**解决的正是同一个问题：很多发送者共用少数几条线路。第二，它很**成熟**，有大量检验过的**路由**（走哪条路）和**调度**（谁什么时候走）方法。第三，**我们是计算机专业的学生**，熟悉这些方法，也熟悉它们的前提。

segs.en: 【指底部深色框】 So our guess was: **borrow routing and scheduling methods from networks, and the robots may finish more orders.** It was only a guess, so we had to test it.
segs.zh: 【指底部深色框】所以我们的猜想是：**借用网络的路由和调度方法，车队也许能完成更多的单。** 这只是猜想，要靠实验检验。

segs.en: Speaker 3 will now explain the model and what we borrowed.
segs.zh: 下面由讲者 3 讲模型和我们借了什么。

title: The model: 16 rooms, 31 links, routers at the doors
hints: Sender / packet / half-duplex link / router port
Router at the door: 4.2×; 30% of waiting on 10% of area
en: Thank you. To borrow network methods, we first needed a model. 【指左图】 We turned the 3,646 walkable cells into a network: **16 rooms become 16 nodes, and 31 doors become 31 links**. 【指红线门 6】 One link stands out: **door 6 is a cut**. Take it away, and the four lower-left rooms are cut off from the rest. 【指右边四行】 The **order center is the sender**. A **robot is a packet**. A **door is a half-duplex link**, a link that carries one direction at a time. The area **within eight steps of a door is the router port**. 【指黄色框】 Why at the door? We measured it. One to three steps from a door, robots spend **4.2 times** as long standing still as moving. The door cell and two steps on each side are **only 10 percent of the area, but hold 30 percent of all waiting**. Time is lost at the door.
zh: 谢谢。要借网络的方法，先要有模型。【指左图】我们把 3646 个可走格子压成一张网络：**16 个房间变成 16 个点，31 道门变成 31 条线**。【指红线门 6】有一条线很特别：**门 6 是一个割**。拿掉它，左下 4 个房间就和其他房间断开了。【指右边四行】逐项对应：**派单中心是发送端**，**机器人是数据包**，**门是半双工链路**，也就是一次只走一个方向的线路；**门口 8 步以内是路由器端口**。【指黄色框】为什么放在门口？我们实测过：离门 1 到 3 步，车停着的时间是走的 **4.2 倍**；门格和两侧各 2 步**只占 10% 的面积，却占了 30% 的等待**。时间就丢在门口。

segs.en: Thank you. To borrow network methods, we first needed a model. 【指左图】 We turned the 3,646 walkable cells into a network: **16 rooms become 16 nodes, and 31 doors become 31 links**.
segs.zh: 谢谢。要借网络的方法，先要有模型。【指左图】我们把 3646 个可走格子压成一张网络：**16 个房间变成 16 个点，31 道门变成 31 条线**。

segs.en: 【指红线门 6】 One link stands out: **door 6 is a cut**. Take it away, and the four lower-left rooms are cut off from the rest.
segs.zh: 【指红线门 6】有一条线很特别：**门 6 是一个割**。拿掉它，左下 4 个房间就和其他房间断开了。

segs.en: 【指右边四行】 The **order center is the sender**. A **robot is a packet**. A **door is a half-duplex link**, a link that carries one direction at a time. The area **within eight steps of a door is the router port**.
segs.zh: 【指右边四行】逐项对应：**派单中心是发送端**，**机器人是数据包**，**门是半双工链路**，也就是一次只走一个方向的线路；**门口 8 步以内是路由器端口**。

segs.en: 【指黄色框】 Why at the door? We measured it. One to three steps from a door, robots spend **4.2 times** as long standing still as moving. The door cell and two steps on each side are **only 10 percent of the area, but hold 30 percent of all waiting**. Time is lost at the door.
segs.zh: 【指黄色框】为什么放在门口？我们实测过：离门 1 到 3 步，车停着的时间是走的 **4.2 倍**；门格和两侧各 2 步**只占 10% 的面积，却占了 30% 的等待**。时间就丢在门口。

title: Similar, but not the same
figs: 图 5 仓库与网络的对应
hints: 4 no retransmission (1986 vs face to face)
Closer to a lossless data-center network
en: But similar is not the same. 【指右边四张卡】 There are four differences. **One: robots cannot be dropped.** A router can throw a packet away. A robot can only wait. **Two: a waiting robot takes up a cell**, and it may block a robot coming the other way. **Three: the number of robots is fixed.** Robots stay on the map after they deliver. **Four: the cause of the jam is different.** The 1986 internet collapse came from **sending the same data again and again**. Here, robots just meet face to face. 【指底部一行】 So we do not borrow methods made for resending. Robots are closer to a **lossless data-center network**, one that never drops data.
zh: 但像不等于一样。【指右边四张卡】有四点不同。**第一，机器人不能丢。** 路由器可以把包扔掉，车只能等。**第二，等着的车占着格子**，可能挡住对面来的车。**第三，车数固定。** 送完货车还在地图上。**第四，堵的原因不同。** 1986 年互联网崩溃来自**同样的数据一遍遍重发**；这里是车面对面顶住。【指底部一行】所以专门对付重发的办法我们不借。机器人更接近数据中心的**无损网络**，也就是从不丢数据的网络。

segs.en: But similar is not the same. 【指右边四张卡】 There are four differences.
segs.zh: 但像不等于一样。【指右边四张卡】有四点不同。

segs.en: **One: robots cannot be dropped.** A router can throw a packet away. A robot can only wait. **Two: a waiting robot takes up a cell**, and it may block a robot coming the other way.
segs.zh: **第一，机器人不能丢。** 路由器可以把包扔掉，车只能等。**第二，等着的车占着格子**，可能挡住对面来的车。

segs.en: **Three: the number of robots is fixed.** Robots stay on the map after they deliver. **Four: the cause of the jam is different.** The 1986 internet collapse came from **sending the same data again and again**. Here, robots just meet face to face.
segs.zh: **第三，车数固定。** 送完货车还在地图上。**第四，堵的原因不同。** 1986 年互联网崩溃来自**同样的数据一遍遍重发**；这里是车面对面顶住。

segs.en: 【指底部一行】 So we do not borrow methods made for resending. Robots are closer to a **lossless data-center network**, one that never drops data.
segs.zh: 【指底部一行】所以专门对付重发的办法我们不借。机器人更接近数据中心的**无损网络**，也就是从不丢数据的网络。

title: Routing or scheduling? The ceiling decides
en: Routing or scheduling? We tried **routing first**. It did not help, and the ceiling, the best possible score, shows why. 【指 1】 The lower-left rooms have **906 of 3,614** room cells: **25 percent**. 【指 2】 An order needs door 6 when its two ends are on different sides. That is **2 times 0.25 times 0.75, which is 37.6 percent**. The task file gives 38.5. 【指 3 和公式】 Door 6 lets through **26 robots every 500 ticks**. So the whole map can finish at most **26 divided by 0.376, which is 69 orders**. No new route can raise it. 【指底部 11】 Later we tested **11 ways to change routes, and all of them were worse**. The real question is **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**. That is scheduling.
zh: 那么，改路由还是改调度？我们**先试了路由**，没用。天花板，也就是最多能做到多少，解释了原因。【指 1】左下房间占 3614 个房间格里的 **906 个**：906 ÷ 3614 = **0.25**，也就是 25%。【指 2】一单两头落在门的两侧，就要过门 6：**2 × 0.25 × 0.75 = 37.6%**，任务文件里核对是 38.5%。【指 3 和公式】门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，所以整张图每 500 拍最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 = 69 单**。换路提高不了它。【指底部 11】后来我们测了 **11 种换路办法，全部变差**。真正的问题是**派多少车、哪边先走**。这是调度。

segs.en: Routing or scheduling? We tried **routing first**. It did not help, and the ceiling, the best possible score, shows why.
segs.zh: 那么，改路由还是改调度？我们**先试了路由**，没用。天花板，也就是最多能做到多少，解释了原因。

segs.en: 【指 1】 The lower-left rooms have **906 of 3,614** room cells: **25 percent**.
【指 2】 An order needs door 6 when its two ends are on different sides. That is **2 times 0.25 times 0.75, which is 37.6 percent**. The task file gives 38.5.
segs.zh: 【指 2】一单两头落在门的两侧，就要过门 6：**2 × 0.25 × 0.75 = 37.6%**，任务文件里核对是 38.5%。

segs.en: 【指 3 和公式】 Door 6 lets through **26 robots every 500 ticks**. So the whole map can finish at most **26 divided by 0.376, which is 69 orders**. No new route can raise it.
segs.zh: 【指 3 和公式】门 6 每 500 拍过 **26 台**，所以整张图每 500 拍最多完成 **26 ÷ 0.376 = 69 单**。换路提高不了它。

segs.en: 【指底部 11】 Later we tested **11 ways to change routes, and all of them were worse**. The real question is **how many robots to send, and which side goes first**. That is scheduling.
segs.zh: 【指底部 11】后来我们测了 **11 种换路办法，全部变差**。真正的问题是**派多少车、哪边先走**。这是调度。

title: Scheduling 1: a per-door quota, like a TCP window
figs: 图 9 在途车与过门数
hints: TCP window: sent but not acknowledged
We count: holds a door-6 order, not crossed, even far away
Full → assign an order that does not cross
Red: 211 in flight, 3 cross; blue: 25 in flight, 26 cross
en: Our first scheduling method is a **quota for each door**. It comes from the **TCP window**. In TCP, the sender limits data that is **sent but not yet confirmed**. We limit robots that **already have an order through door 6 but have not crossed yet**, even if they are far away. 【指右边三条】 When the quota is full, the center gives that robot **an order that does not use the door**. 【指黄色框】 The quota size is **bandwidth times delay**: a slowdown of **2.23** from breakdowns, times **247 ticks** to reach the door, divided by 500, times **13 robots per 500 ticks** in each direction. That gives **15 going in and 10 going out**. Unlike TCP, **nothing is dropped and the quota is fixed**, so we had to test it. 【指左图红线】 In red, with no control, robots on the way to the door climb to **211**, and only **3** get through every 500 ticks. 【指蓝点】 In blue, with the quota, about **25** are on the way, and the door lets through **26 on average**. Too many robots do not go faster. **They get stuck.**
zh: 第一个调度方法是**每门名额**。它借自 **TCP 窗口**：TCP 里，发送端限制**已经发出、还没确认**的数据。我们限制**已经接了要过门 6 的单、还没过门**的车，哪怕它离门还很远。【指右边三条】名额满了，派单中心就给这台车派**一单不过门的**。【指黄色框】名额大小按**带宽乘时延**算：故障放慢 **2.23** × 走到门口 **247 拍** ÷ 500 × 每个方向每 500 拍 **13 台**，得到**进 15 台、出 10 台**。和 TCP 不同，**这里不丢包、名额固定**，所以有没有用必须实验检验。【指左图红线】红线不管门，在途车涨到 **211 台**，每 500 拍只过 **3 台**。【指蓝点】蓝点用名额，在途 25 台左右，门平均过 **26 台**。车放多了不会过得更快，**只会堵死**。

segs.en: We limit robots that **already have an order through door 6 but have not crossed yet**, even if they are far away. 【指右边三条】 When the quota is full, the center gives that robot **an order that does not use the door**.
segs.zh: 我们限制**已经接了要过门 6 的单、还没过门**的车，哪怕它离门还很远。【指右边三条】名额满了，派单中心就给这台车派**一单不过门的**。

segs.en: 【指黄色框】 The quota size is **bandwidth times delay**: a slowdown of **2.23** from breakdowns, times **247 ticks** to reach the door, divided by 500, times **13 robots per 500 ticks** in each direction. That gives **15 going in and 10 going out**.
segs.zh: 【指黄色框】名额大小按**带宽乘时延**算：故障放慢 **2.23** × 走到门口 **247 拍** ÷ 500 × 每个方向每 500 拍 **13 台**，得到**进 15 台、出 10 台**。

segs.en: Unlike TCP, **nothing is dropped and the quota is fixed**, so we had to test it.
segs.zh: 和 TCP 不同，**这里不丢包、名额固定**，所以有没有用必须实验检验。

segs.en: 【指左图红线】 In red, with no control, robots on the way to the door climb to **211**, and only **3** get through every 500 ticks. 【指蓝点】 In blue, with the quota, about **25** are on the way, and the door lets through **26 on average**. Too many robots do not go faster. **They get stuck.**
segs.zh: 【指左图红线】红线不管门，在途车涨到 **211 台**，每 500 拍只过 **3 台**。【指蓝点】蓝点用名额，在途 25 台左右，门平均过 **26 台**。车放多了不会过得更快，**只会堵死**。

title: Scheduling 2: one side at a time, switch when empty
hints: Serve one side → drain → switch, no timer
en: The second method is the **door rule**. It comes from **half-duplex links and polling**, which means serving each side in turn. A one-cell door is a half-duplex link: **one direction at a time**. We measured two costs. In the same direction, a robot follows every **9 ticks**. But changing direction takes **21 ticks**, because the door and the other side must clear first. 【指 43%】 If the door changes direction after every robot, it is busy only **9 out of 21, or 43 percent** of the time. 【指 88%】 With groups of ten, it is **90 out of 102, or 88 percent**. 【指上面三格图，从左到右】 So the door serves one side. When that side is empty, it finishes, and then it changes direction. **No timer is needed.** 【指 4 cells】 One rule has **nothing like it in networks**: robots on the other side **step back out of a four-cell zone**, so the exit stays clear. A waiting packet never blocks a cable, but **a waiting robot blocks the way**.
zh: 第二个方法是**门口规则**，借自**半双工链路和轮询**，也就是两边轮流服务。一格宽的门就是半双工链路：**一次一个方向**。我们测了两个代价：同方向每 **9 拍**跟过一台；换方向要 **21 拍**，因为门格和对面要先清空。【指 43%】每过一台就换向，门只有 **9 ÷ 21 = 43%** 的时间在过车。【指 88%】一批放 10 台，是 **90 ÷ 102 = 88%**。【指上面三格图，从左到右】所以门先服务一边，这一边走空了就收尾，然后换向，**不需要定时器**。【指 4 cells】还有一条规则**网络里没有**：对面的车**退出 4 格的门口区**，把出口让出来。等着的数据包不会挡住网线，但**等着的车会挡路**。

segs.en: The second method is the **door rule**. It comes from **half-duplex links and polling**, which means serving each side in turn. A one-cell door is a half-duplex link: **one direction at a time**.
segs.zh: 第二个方法是**门口规则**，借自**半双工链路和轮询**，也就是两边轮流服务。一格宽的门就是半双工链路：**一次一个方向**。

segs.en: We measured two costs. In the same direction, a robot follows every **9 ticks**. But changing direction takes **21 ticks**, because the door and the other side must clear first.
segs.zh: 我们测了两个代价：同方向每 **9 拍**跟过一台；换方向要 **21 拍**，因为门格和对面要先清空。

segs.en: 【指 43%】 If the door changes direction after every robot, it is busy only **9 out of 21, or 43 percent** of the time. 【指 88%】 With groups of ten, it is **90 out of 102, or 88 percent**.
【指上面三格图，从左到右】 So the door serves one side. When that side is empty, it finishes, and then it changes direction. **No timer is needed.**
segs.zh: 【指上面三格图，从左到右】所以门先服务一边，这一边走空了就收尾，然后换向，**不需要定时器**。

segs.en: 【指 4 cells】 One rule has **nothing like it in networks**: robots on the other side **step back out of a four-cell zone**, so the exit stays clear. A waiting packet never blocks a cable, but **a waiting robot blocks the way**.
segs.zh: 【指 4 cells】还有一条规则**网络里没有**：对面的车**退出 4 格的门口区**，把出口让出来。等着的数据包不会挡住网线，但**等着的车会挡路**。

title: A bug fix and two safety nets
figs: 图 12 执行器修复示意
hints: Credit flow control: return a freed slot at once
Executor kept robot in old cell's queue
Watchdog 300 ticks; relax rule, never drop
en: Third, a **bug fix**. Even with both rules, door 6 was **stuck at 22** robots every 500 ticks. In **credit flow control**, when a slot is free, the sender must be told **at once**. 【指上排】 We checked tick by tick. The official executor **kept a robot in a cell's waiting list after it had left the cell**. So the next robot waited a whole planning round for nothing. 【指下排和 22 → 26】 We changed **three lines**, and the door went back to **26**. 【指右上】 Last, **two safety nets**. The first is a **global cap** from Little's law: 1.76 times 69.2 divided by 500, times 2.23, times 255, gives **138 robots** with orders at most. 【指右下】 The second is a **deadlock watchdog**, from lossless networks. If a robot has waited **300 ticks**, and no robot has entered its door for 300 ticks, it may skip the door rule for one tick. Switches drop packets to break a deadlock. **We cannot drop robots, so we relax the rule instead.** Speaker 4 will show the results.
zh: 第三是**修一个程序错误**。两条规则都上了，门 6 还是**卡在每 500 拍 22 台**。**信用流控**里，空位一腾出来就要**立刻**告诉发送端。【指上排】一拍一拍查下来，发现官方执行器**在车离开一格后，那一格的排队名单里还留着它**，后面的车白等一整个规划周期。【指下排和 22 → 26】改了 **3 行**，门回到 **26 台**。【指右上】最后是**两个兜底**。第一个是按 Little 定律定的**全图上限**：1.76 × 69.2 ÷ 500 × 2.23 × 255，得到同时接单最多 **138 台**。【指右下】第二个是借自无损网络的**死锁看门狗**：车等满 **300 拍**、它所在的门 300 拍没有车进，就允许它这一拍不守门口规则。交换机靠丢包走出死锁，**我们不能丢车，所以改成放宽规则**。下面讲者 4 讲结果。

segs.en: Third, a **bug fix**. Even with both rules, door 6 was **stuck at 22** robots every 500 ticks. In **credit flow control**, when a slot is free, the sender must be told **at once**.
segs.zh: 第三是**修一个程序错误**。两条规则都上了，门 6 还是**卡在每 500 拍 22 台**。**信用流控**里，空位一腾出来就要**立刻**告诉发送端。

segs.en: 【指上排】 We checked tick by tick. The official executor **kept a robot in a cell's waiting list after it had left the cell**. So the next robot waited a whole planning round for nothing.
segs.zh: 【指上排】一拍一拍查下来，发现官方执行器**在车离开一格后，那一格的排队名单里还留着它**，后面的车白等一整个规划周期。

segs.en: 【指下排和 22 → 26】 We changed **three lines**, and the door went back to **26**.
【指右上】 Last, **two safety nets**. The first is a **global cap** from Little's law: 1.76 times 69.2 divided by 500, times 2.23, times 255, gives **138 robots** with orders at most.
segs.zh: 【指右上】最后是**两个兜底**。第一个是按 Little 定律定的**全图上限**：1.76 × 69.2 ÷ 500 × 2.23 × 255，得到同时接单最多 **138 台**。

segs.en: 【指右下】 The second is a **deadlock watchdog**, from lossless networks. If a robot has waited **300 ticks**, and no robot has entered its door for 300 ticks, it may skip the door rule for one tick. Switches drop packets to break a deadlock. **We cannot drop robots, so we relax the rule instead.**
segs.zh: 【指右下】第二个是借自无损网络的**死锁看门狗**：车等满 **300 拍**、它所在的门 300 拍没有车进，就允许它这一拍不守门口规则。交换机靠丢包走出死锁，**我们不能丢车，所以改成放宽规则**。

segs.en: Speaker 4 will show the results.
segs.zh: 下面讲者 4 讲结果。

title: Results on the official room map
figs: 图 14 逐级结果柱状图
hints: Bars: starter → champion → fixed executor → ours
All 8 official instances: +113.6%; no harm where off
en: Thank you. Here are the results on the **official room map**: three fleet sizes, **20 runs** each, 5,000 ticks per run. 【指柱状图，从灰到橙】 Each group of bars adds one step: the official starter program, the champion's assignment, the fixed executor, and last, in orange, our door control. 【指 +140.5%】 Compared with the official starter program, finished orders go up by **140.5 percent**. 【指 +76.5%】 But the **fairest comparison** is with the same champion assignment and the same fixed executor. Then the only difference is our control. The gain is **76.5 percent**. 【指 618 → 1,106】 With 250 robots, each run goes from **618 orders to 1,106**. 【指底部小字】 If we count all eight official instances, the gain is **113.6 percent**. That includes maze, random and warehouse maps, where our control **never turns on**. On those maps the results stay the same, so the method does no harm where it is not needed.
zh: 谢谢。这是**官方房间图**上的结果：三种车数，每种 **20 局**，每局 5000 拍。【指柱状图，从灰到橙】每组柱子逐级加一步：官方起始程序、冠军派单、修好执行器，最后橙色是加上我们的门控。【指 +140.5%】比官方起始程序，完成数多了 **140.5%**。【指 +76.5%】但**最公平的比较**是和同样冠军派单、同样修好执行器的程序比，这时只差我们的控制：多了 **76.5%**。【指 618 → 1,106】250 台车时，每局**从 618 单到 1106 单**。【指底部小字】如果算官方全部 8 个实例，是 **+113.6%**。这里面包括迷宫、随机图、仓库图，我们的控制在这些图上**根本不启动**，结果和原来一样，说明用不着的地方不添乱。

segs.en: Thank you. Here are the results on the **official room map**: three fleet sizes, **20 runs** each, 5,000 ticks per run.
segs.zh: 谢谢。这是**官方房间图**上的结果：三种车数，每种 **20 局**，每局 5000 拍。

segs.en: 【指柱状图，从灰到橙】 Each group of bars adds one step: the official starter program, the champion's assignment, the fixed executor, and last, in orange, our door control.
segs.zh: 【指柱状图，从灰到橙】每组柱子逐级加一步：官方起始程序、冠军派单、修好执行器，最后橙色是加上我们的门控。

segs.en: 【指 +140.5%】 Compared with the official starter program, finished orders go up by **140.5 percent**. 【指 +76.5%】 But the **fairest comparison** is with the same champion assignment and the same fixed executor. Then the only difference is our control. The gain is **76.5 percent**.
segs.zh: 【指 +140.5%】比官方起始程序，完成数多了 **140.5%**。【指 +76.5%】但**最公平的比较**是和同样冠军派单、同样修好执行器的程序比，这时只差我们的控制：多了 **76.5%**。

segs.en: 【指 618 → 1,106】 With 250 robots, each run goes from **618 orders to 1,106**.

【指底部小字】 If we count all eight official instances, the gain is **113.6 percent**. That includes maze, random and warehouse maps, where our control **never turns on**. On those maps the results stay the same, so the method does no harm where it is not needed.
segs.zh: 【指底部小字】如果算官方全部 8 个实例，是 **+113.6%**。这里面包括迷宫、随机图、仓库图，我们的控制在这些图上**根本不启动**，结果和原来一样，说明用不着的地方不添乱。

title: What matters, and does it work on other maps?
figs: 图 16 逐项拿掉与加上
hints: Door rule alone +29.7, quota alone +29.3, together +76.4
Quota = how many; door rule = how they pass
Remove global cap: −16.9% on one map
en: Which parts matter? 【指左边红条】 We ran **600 games** again and took out one part at a time. Without the **door rule, we lose 25.6 percent**. Without the **quota, 13.6**. Without the **executor fix, 6.7**. 【指右边蓝条】 Added alone, the door rule gives **29.7 percent** and the quota **29.3**. Together they give **76.4**. 【指黄框】 **The quota decides how many robots come. The door rule decides how they pass.** 【指右上 +86.9%】 We also worried that our method only fits this one map. So we wrote a program to make **eight new room maps with random doors**. The full method **won on every one**, by **86.9 percent** on average. 【指 −16.9%】 The global cap shows no effect on the official map. But on one new map, taking it out costs **16.9 percent**. That is why we keep the safety nets.
zh: 哪些部分起作用？【指左边红条】我们重跑了 **600 局**，每次拿掉一项：拿掉**门口规则少 25.6%**，拿掉**名额少 13.6%**，拿掉**执行器修复少 6.7%**。【指右边蓝条】单独加上门口规则 **+29.7%**，单独加上名额 **+29.3%**；两个一起是 **+76.4%**。【指黄框】**名额管来多少车，门口规则管来了怎么过。**【指右上 +86.9%】我们还担心方法只适合这一张图，于是写了生成程序，造了 **8 张随机门的新房间图**。完整方法**每张都赢**，平均 **+86.9%**。【指 −16.9%】全图上限在官方图上测不出作用，但在一张新图上拿掉它会少 **16.9%**，所以兜底要留着。

segs.en: Which parts matter? 【指左边红条】 We ran **600 games** again and took out one part at a time. Without the **door rule, we lose 25.6 percent**. Without the **quota, 13.6**. Without the **executor fix, 6.7**.
segs.zh: 哪些部分起作用？【指左边红条】我们重跑了 **600 局**，每次拿掉一项：拿掉**门口规则少 25.6%**，拿掉**名额少 13.6%**，拿掉**执行器修复少 6.7%**。

segs.en: 【指右边蓝条】 Added alone, the door rule gives **29.7 percent** and the quota **29.3**. Together they give **76.4**.
segs.zh: 【指右边蓝条】单独加上门口规则 **+29.7%**，单独加上名额 **+29.3%**；两个一起是 **+76.4%**。

segs.en: 【指黄框】 **The quota decides how many robots come. The door rule decides how they pass.**
segs.zh: 【指黄框】**名额管来多少车，门口规则管来了怎么过。**

segs.en: 【指右上 +86.9%】 We also worried that our method only fits this one map. So we wrote a program to make **eight new room maps with random doors**. The full method **won on every one**, by **86.9 percent** on average.
segs.zh: 【指右上 +86.9%】我们还担心方法只适合这一张图，于是写了生成程序，造了 **8 张随机门的新房间图**。完整方法**每张都赢**，平均 **+86.9%**。

segs.en: 【指 −16.9%】 The global cap shows no effect on the official map. But on one new map, taking it out costs **16.9 percent**. That is why we keep the safety nets.
segs.zh: 【指 −16.9%】全图上限在官方图上测不出作用，但在一张新图上拿掉它会少 **16.9%**，所以兜底要留着。

title: Most ideas failed, and why
figs: 图 18 69 项机制的筛选漏斗
hints: Lessons: assumptions break; door 6 sets throughput; confirm on new maps
en: Most of our ideas failed, and we want to be honest about it. 【指漏斗从上到下】 In the protocol phase, we wrote down **69 network ideas**. **38** stopped after a first quick measurement. **23** failed the development tests. **7** passed development but were not confirmed on new maps. **Only one**, the watchdog, passed. **Every way of changing routes lost.** 【指三张卡】 We learned three things. **What network methods assume often fails for robots**, because robots cannot be dropped and they take up cells. **Door 6 sets how many orders we can finish.** And **gains on test maps must be checked again on new maps.**
zh: 我们的大多数想法都失败了，这一点要如实讲。【指漏斗从上到下】协议阶段我们一共写下 **69 种网络机制**。**38 种**先量一下就放弃了，**23 种**没过开发测试，**7 种**过了开发但在新图上没确认，**只有看门狗 1 种**通过。**所有换路办法都变差。**【指三张卡】我们学到三点：**网络方法的前提在机器人上常常不成立**，因为车不能丢、还占格子；**完成多少单由门 6 决定**；**开发图上的提升必须换新图再确认。**

title: Conclusion
hints: Not smarter robots: count + which side
Hypothesis half right: routing no, scheduling yes
Real warehouse: quota per direction + one direction at a time
Simulation only; re-measure for new layouts
en: To finish. 【指 1】 **We did not make each robot smarter.** We managed the warehouse like a network: **how many robots go to a door, and which side the door serves.** 【指 2】 Our guess was **half right**: **routing did not carry over, but scheduling did.** 【指 3】 In a real warehouse with a narrow aisle, this means **a quota for each direction, counted when orders are given out, and one direction at a time in the aisle.** 【指 4】 Our limits: all results come **from simulation**, and the numbers must be **measured again for a new layout**. Thank you. We are happy to take your questions.
zh: 总结一下。【指 1】**我们没有让每台车更聪明**，而是像管网络一样，管住**多少车奔向一道门、这道门先放哪边**。【指 2】我们的猜想**对了一半**：**路由搬不过来，调度有效。**【指 3】在有窄巷的真实仓库里，就是**每个方向一个名额，派单时就算；巷口一次只放一个方向。**【指 4】局限：所有结果都**来自仿真**，换一种布局要**重新测参数**。谢谢大家，欢迎提问。

segs.en: To finish. 【指 1】 **We did not make each robot smarter.** We managed the warehouse like a network: **how many robots go to a door, and which side the door serves.**

segs.en: 【指 2】 Our guess was **half right**: **routing did not carry over, but scheduling did.**
segs.zh: 【指 2】我们的猜想**对了一半**：**路由搬不过来，调度有效。**

segs.en: 【指 3】 In a real warehouse with a narrow aisle, this means **a quota for each direction, counted when orders are given out, and one direction at a time in the aisle.**
segs.zh: 【指 3】在有窄巷的真实仓库里，就是**每个方向一个名额，派单时就算；巷口一次只放一个方向。**

segs.en: 【指 4】 Our limits: all results come **from simulation**, and the numbers must be **measured again for a new layout**.
segs.zh: 【指 4】局限：所有结果都**来自仿真**，换一种布局要**重新测参数**。

segs.en: Thank you. We are happy to take your questions.
segs.zh: 谢谢大家，欢迎提问。
